notes: CIRCUIT: five op-amp stages, same generator family as circuit_744. Stage A (op-amp #3) is fed directly by the 5V source #6 with C0 (1uF) as feedback; its output drives R4 (1k) into stage B (op-amp #2, L1 1uH feedback), whose output goes through R5 (1k) to a common right-hand rail (the slanted line down the right edge, x~990 at the top to x~940 at the bottom). Stage C (op-amp #12) is fed by the 10A source #15 with L10 (1uH) feedback; its output runs right along y~575, crosses the x~455 column at S26 and continues through R14 (1k) into stage D (op-amp #11, C9 1uF feedback). The x~455 column carries that same node up to the in+ of stage B and down to C22 (1uF) which feeds stage E (op-amp #20, L19 1uH feedback). Outputs of D and E reach the right rail through R13 and R21. NET MAP: '0' = ground: bottom of V-DC #6, bottom of I-DC #15, the non-inverting (+) inputs of op-amps #3/#11/#12/#20, and GNDs #7,#8,#16,#17,#18,#23. n1 = top of V-DC #6 (121,210), the y~186 wire, the in- of op-amp #3 and the left plate of C0 (the left leg runs (244,125)->(197,185)). n2 = output of op-amp #3 (291,201), right plate of C0 (down at x~356), left end of R4. n3 = right end of R4, in- (top-left lead) of op-amp #2, left leg of L1 (down at x~491). n4 = output of op-amp #2 (595,229), right leg of L1 (down at x~676), left end of R5. n5 = output of op-amp #12 (298,575), right end of L10, the whole x~455 column from y~290 down to y~845, the in+ (bottom-left lead) of op-amp #2, left end of R14, left plate of C22. n6 = the right-hand rail: right ends of R5, R13 and R21 only (3-terminal floating summing node, as drawn). n7 = output of op-amp #11 (732,600), right plate of C9 (down at x~787), left end of R13. n8 = right end of R14, in- of op-amp #11, left plate of C9 (down at x~610). n9 = top of I-DC #15, in- of op-amp #12, left leg of L10 (down at x~190). n10 = right plate of C22, in- of op-amp #20, left leg of L19 (down at x~576). n11 = output of op-amp #20 (689,856), right leg of L19 (down at x~767), left end of R21. SITES: twelve sites recorded, all junctions. S3 (197,188), S4 (356,203), S8 (491,216), S10 (676,232), S22 (190,557), S28 (343,577), S29 (610,586), S30 (787,599), S36 (576,846), S37 (767,856) are all clean T-intersections where the leg of a feedback element (C0, L1, L10, C9, L19) lands on a horizontal wire; the leg terminates there, so reading any of them as a crossing would leave that feedback element on a one-terminal net - impossible. S3 is only load-bearing after the port fix on C0 below (the tracer had C0's left terminal on label ink, so it did not flag S3 as CRITICAL); with the fix it carries the V-DC top, C0's left plate and op-amp #3's in- onto one node, which is what the ink shows (edges e13 (126,185)->(194,188), e8 (244,125)->(197,185) and e14 (200,189)->(240,191) all meet there). S32 (958,608) is a T where the horizontal out of R13 lands on the slanted right rail; the rail is the last ink on the right so a crossing would strand R13's right terminal alone. S26 (457,574) is the only genuine 4-way and the one real judgement call: inkmap at (457,574) shows the x~455 column running straight through, the wire from op-amp #12's output arriving from the left at y~577 and the wire on to R14 leaving at y~574 - i.e. the two horizontal arms are drawn as separate strokes each ending on the column, offset by only ~3 px, with no solder blob (the patch is no fatter than the 3 px strokes) and no hop or jog anywhere. I read it as a JUNCTION: (a) nothing on this sheet is drawn with a hop, so by the ink prior a plain crossing means connected; (b) the identical node in the sibling drawing circuit_744 (same topology, same values) is drawn with an explicit solder ring; (c) the crossing reading would split n5 into {op-amp #12 out, L10 right, R14 left} and {op-amp #2 in+, C22 left}, leaving the in+ of stage B and the whole of stage E driven by nothing at all - a branch with no source and no return path. Non-critical sites S0, S1, S2, S5, S6, S11, S20, S25, S27, S34, S35 are handwritten value text ('1uF', '1uH', '1k ohm', '5v') brushing a wire or a component box and were left at the tracer default. PORT FIXES: (1) Capacitor #0 had t0 on a 3 px stub of the '1uF' label at (284,89) (one-terminal net n1); its real left plate lead is port p1 at (244,125) with a 112 px wire running left and down to the op-amp #3 input node, so t0 -> p1. (2) V-DC #6 had BOTH terminals sitting on strokes of the handwritten '5v' label at (83,253) and (88,242), which shorted the source onto a single 2-terminal net; its real leads are port p2 at (121,210) going up to the y~186 wire and port p3 at (119,284) going down into GND #8, so t0 -> p2 and t1 -> p3. That fix also removes the spurious one-terminal net n6 (op-amp #3's in-), which had nothing else on it only because the source and the capacitor were both parked on text. (3) Pin order on all five op-amps: every one is drawn with '-' on the upper input and '+' on the lower input, and every one has its feedback element returning to the upper lead, confirming the marks. #2: t0->p0 (bottom '+'), t1->p2 (top '-'), t2->p1 (apex/out). #3, #11, #12: t0->p2 (bottom '+'), t1->p1 (top '-'), t2->p0 (out). #20: t0->p3 (607,872) - the '+' lead leaving the triangle's flat side, which runs down to GND #23; the tracer had used p2 (607,910), the far end of the very same edge e84, so the net is unchanged - t1->p1 (top '-'), t2->p0 (out). No class looks wrong (5 Op-Amps, 5 Resistors, 3 Capacitors, 3 Inductors, 1 V-DC, 1 I-DC, 6 GND). UNRESOLVED: nothing outstanding.
